title: The Missing Project Aurora Document
briefing: At 10:18, an external recipient received the confidential Aurora launch document. Five employees had authorized read access. Determine who disclosed it, how, and why. All times are office-local; systems were synchronized to within two seconds.

suspects.name: Maya Chen
suspects.profile: Owned the launch draft and chaired the morning review.

suspects.name: Daniel Brooks
suspects.profile: Negotiated launch partnerships; had a disputed referral payment.

suspects.name: Priya Shah
suspects.profile: Audited document access; investigated an alert.

suspects.name: Ethan Cole
suspects.profile: Maintained a service account and the print system.

suspects.name: Sofia Reyes
suspects.profile: Prepared slides and booked the review room.

evidence.title: Document audit
evidence.body: 09:42 Maya read v7 on L-01; 09:51 Daniel downloaded v7 on L-17; 10:04 Priya read v7 on S-02. No other v7 downloads occurred before 10:18.

evidence.title: Disclosure report
evidence.body: At 10:18 receiver northstar-drop@example.test acknowledged Aurora v7, including its confidential pricing appendix. This is a fictional internal exercise address.

evidence.title: Morning calendar
evidence.body: Maya and Sofia attended a recorded review from 09:55–10:25. Daniel was invited but declined. Ethan had a maintenance window at 10:00.

evidence.title: Access holders
evidence.body: All five suspects could read Aurora. External transfer required separate approval. No external transfer was approved that morning.

evidence.title: Transfer gateway
evidence.body: 10:12 L-17 uploaded aurora-v7.pdf to the external Northstar drop. Device certificate D-17 authenticated the transfer. Digest matched the disclosed file.

evidence.title: Device inventory
evidence.body: L-17 and non-exportable device certificate D-17 were assigned to Daniel. L-17 could not be accessed remotely during the incident; remote desktop was disabled.

evidence.title: Service account
evidence.body: Ethan’s service account printed a diagnostic cover sheet at 10:01 on P-04. It had no permission to read or transfer Aurora; no document payload was printed.

evidence.title: Referral message
evidence.body: At 09:35 Daniel messaged Northstar: “The launch pricing appendix will settle my referral payment.” Finance confirms a disputed personal referral fee.

evidence.title: Reception testimony
evidence.body: Receptionist Lena saw Daniel carrying L-17 into the east booth at 10:07. She recognized his name badge and spoke to him about a parcel.

evidence.title: Security testimony
evidence.body: Priya opened v7 at 10:04 to compare its watermark after a transfer-preparation alert. Her workstation remained on the security VLAN; gateway records show no outbound document from S-02.

evidence.title: CCTV sequence
evidence.body: 10:06 Daniel leaves the lobby, enters the east booth at 10:07, exits 10:14 holding L-17. The booth had one entrance and no other visitor during that interval.

evidence.title: Contradictory alibi
evidence.body: Daniel claimed he was with reception continuously from 10:00–10:20. Parcel and CCTV records put him away from reception during the transfer. Meeting recording places Maya and Sofia in the review; Ethan’s console log and camera place him at P-04.

0.prompt: Who downloaded v7 before the incident?

1.prompt: Which device sent the disclosed file?
What ties the transfer to the disclosed document?
What does the service-account activity establish?

2.prompt: Which alibi contradicts the witness account?
Why did Priya read the document?

options: External upload from L-17 in the east booth
Matching digest and D-17 transfer, with CCTV placing Daniel at L-17

4.answer: External upload from L-17 in the east booth
Matching digest and D-17 transfer, with CCTV placing Daniel at L-17

exchanges.question: Who used the east booth?
exchanges.response: Daniel, carrying his laptop. I spoke to him at 10:07.

exchanges.question: Was he at reception throughout the interval?
Why open the file?
exchanges.response: To compare the watermark for an alert, not to export it.

exchanges.question: Could Ethan’s account read it?
exchanges.response: No. The service account only had print-diagnostic permission.

events.label: Daniel enters the east booth at 10:07

solution: Daniel Brooks disclosed Aurora v7 to secure his disputed personal referral payment. He downloaded the document on L-17 at 09:51 and used the east booth to upload it at 10:12. The matching file digest and non-exportable device certificate connect the disclosed file to his laptop; CCTV and Lena place him with that laptop in the booth. His reception alibi is false. Priya’s read was an audit, Ethan’s service activity printed only a diagnostic, and Maya and Sofia were on the recorded review. No accomplice is needed.

title: The Vanishing Prototype
briefing: A sensor prototype vanished from a locked lab before an 11:00 customer demonstration. The exit alarm never sounded. Investigate the five authorized staff, the decoy parcel, and the movement of the real unit.

suspects.name: Alex Morgan
suspects.profile: Needed the unit for a customer demo.

suspects.name: Nora Patel
suspects.profile: Faced penalties if the demo exposed inflated performance claims.

evidence.title: Inventory
evidence.body: Prototype serial AUR-9 was verified in locker L2 at 09:00. AUR-9 has a passive RFID tag; the spare enclosure is empty and tagged DUMMY-1.

evidence.title: Lab access
evidence.body: 09:10 Leo enters for calibration; 09:30 Alex enters; 09:40 Nora enters alone; 10:10 Owen enters accompanied by security. Iris never enters.

evidence.title: Demonstration booking
evidence.body: Customer demo booked for 11:00. Nora owns the published performance claims. Alex reported discrepancies at 08:50.

evidence.title: Exit policy
evidence.body: The lab door reader logs AUR-9 when carried across the threshold. It did not log AUR-9 after 09:00. The internal storage hatch does not cross that threshold.

evidence.title: Locker audit
evidence.body: 09:43 Nora’s unique badge opened L2. At 09:45 the adjacent internal storage hatch was opened using the same badge.

evidence.title: Return parcel
evidence.body: Iris dispatched a supplier box at 09:55. Packing scan shows only DUMMY-1 and return screws. Carrier weighing and the photographed seal match the empty enclosure.

evidence.title: Internal RFID
evidence.body: AUR-9 detected in storage compartment C at 09:46, then remained there. Compartment C is reachable only through the internal hatch; no corridor entrance exists.

evidence.title: Private message
evidence.body: 09:05 Nora to a colleague: “A no-show buys time; a live demo proves I inflated the range. I need it unavailable until tomorrow.”

evidence.title: Technician testimony
evidence.body: Leo verified AUR-9 in L2 at 09:25 after calibration and left at 09:26. Security footage confirms his departure.

evidence.title: Facilities testimony
evidence.body: Owen and security entered at 10:10 for ventilation work. They never opened storage. Security’s continuous body camera confirms this.

evidence.title: CCTV
evidence.body: 09:40 Nora enters with empty hands, 09:47 leaves with empty hands. At 09:44 the lab camera shows her lifting AUR-9 toward the storage hatch. Alex left at 09:35.

evidence.title: Recovery
evidence.body: At 10:40 security opened compartment C and recovered intact AUR-9 beneath a dust cover. Its serial and tag match inventory. No theft through a lab exit occurred.

0.prompt: Which serial is the real prototype?
Did the real unit cross the lab door?

1.prompt: Whose badge opened L2 and the hatch?
What was in the return parcel?

2.prompt: Who verified AUR-9 before Nora arrived?
Where did security recover the unit?

options: Postpone exposure of inflated demo claims
Hide AUR-9 through the internal hatch in compartment C
Ship AUR-9 in the supplier box
Carry AUR-9 out the lab door
Nora’s badge sequence, movement on CCTV and RFID in C

4.answer: Postpone exposure of inflated demo claims
Hide AUR-9 through the internal hatch in compartment C
Nora’s badge sequence, movement on CCTV and RFID in C

exchanges.question: Where did you leave the prototype?
Did you use the hatch?
exchanges.response: No; calibration was on the lab bench.

exchanges.question: Where was AUR-9 found?
exchanges.response: Inside compartment C, not in the return parcel.

solution: Nora Patel hid AUR-9 in internal compartment C to postpone a demo that would expose her inflated range claims. Her badge opened both L2 and the hatch; CCTV records the movement and RFID locates the unit in C at 09:46. Because the unit never crossed the lab door, there was no exit alert. Iris shipped a documented dummy enclosure, Leo left the real unit locked after calibration, Alex departed before the removal, and Owen arrived later under continuous supervision.

title: The Impossible Meeting
briefing: An apparently unanimous purchasing approval was recorded during a meeting that three invitees say never happened. Identify who fabricated the approval and reconcile the contradictory attendance and audit records.

suspects.name: Grace Lin
suspects.profile: Required live consent for a large purchase.

suspects.name: Marcus Vale
suspects.profile: Was close to losing a personal vendor bonus.

suspects.name: Amira Khan
suspects.profile: Was due to review the vendor contract.

evidence.title: Approval record
evidence.body: Minutes claim all five staff approved the vendor at 14:00 in Cedar. Policy requires live unanimous approval; an invitation or bot transcript is not consent.

evidence.title: Calendar audit
evidence.body: Tessa booked Cedar for 14:00. At 13:40 Marcus alone changed the invite to a remote link and removed the room reservation.

evidence.title: Room access
evidence.body: Cedar was locked for maintenance 13:50–14:30. Security logged only Ben and an escort; no purchasing attendees entered.

evidence.title: Attendance objections
evidence.body: Grace, Tessa and Amira independently reported receiving a cancellation notice at 13:41. None joined a call at 14:00.

evidence.title: Conference audit
evidence.body: At 14:00 only Marcus and the auto-caption bot joined the remote link. The server recorded one human attendee; the bot cannot approve purchases.

evidence.title: Document history
evidence.body: At 14:12 Marcus’s authenticated session created minutes claiming five approvals. No earlier draft or uploaded recording exists. Document history is append-only.

evidence.title: Notification audit
evidence.body: 13:41 Marcus used the organizer controls delegated for this meeting to send cancellation notices to Grace, Tessa and Amira, while retaining his remote link.

evidence.title: Vendor incentive
evidence.body: Marcus was promised a personal vendor bonus if approval arrived that day. Finance had not authorized that bonus. He wrote at 13:35: “No time for another review.”

evidence.title: Assistant testimony
evidence.body: Tessa booked the original room but delegated change controls to Marcus at his request. She received cancellation and did not attend.

evidence.title: IT testimony
evidence.body: Ben performed physical maintenance with an escort. No conference-account impersonation or credential reset took place. Server timestamps are synchronized.

evidence.title: Submission audit
evidence.body: At 14:15 Marcus submitted the new minutes to purchasing as unanimous consent. The server attributed document creation and submission to the same authenticated session.

evidence.title: Reconciliation
evidence.body: A caption bot generated only a “meeting started” marker, not votes or a transcript. The empty room and one-human remote call are compatible; the five approvals in Marcus’s minutes are unsupported.

1.prompt: How many human attendees joined remotely?

options: Obtain a personal vendor bonus before deadline
Cancel attendees and fabricate unanimous minutes after joining alone
Use the bot to cast valid votes
One-human attendance plus Marcus’s append-only creation and submission audit

4.answer: Obtain a personal vendor bonus before deadline
Cancel attendees and fabricate unanimous minutes after joining alone
One-human attendance plus Marcus’s append-only creation and submission audit

exchanges.question: Did you approve the purchase?
exchanges.response: No. I received cancellation and attended no meeting.

exchanges.question: Who controlled changes?
exchanges.response: Marcus had delegated organizer controls for that meeting.

exchanges.question: Was the room occupied by attendees?
Could the bot vote?
exchanges.response: No. It records captions; it has no purchasing authority.

solution: Marcus Vale fabricated unanimous purchasing approval to obtain a personal vendor bonus before its deadline. He redirected the invitation, cancelled other attendees, joined alone, then authored and submitted false minutes. Server attendance, notification records and append-only document history resolve the apparent impossibility: the original room was empty and the remote meeting had one human. Tessa merely created the original invitation; Ben’s maintenance explains the locked room, and Grace and Amira never consented. The caption bot supplied no votes.
